# stdlib_breadth_targets.txt — the oracle-checked call corpus for the
# `beam_engine` corpus-breadth suite (`tests/stdlib_lists.rs`,
# `breadth_runs_a_large_fraction_of_the_installed_corpus`).
#
# Every line is
#
#     <module>:<function>(<args>) => <expected>   # oracle: erl -noshell -eval '<command>'
#
# where `<expected>` is the **verbatim `~w` rendering the real system Erlang
# (OTP 29 / erts-17.1) produced** for `Module:Function(Args)`, and the trailing
# comment quotes the exact `erl -noshell -eval …` invocation that produces it
# (copy-paste it to re-verify any single entry).  No value here was guessed and
# none was derived from the Rust engine's own output.
#
# The corpus was generated by evaluating every expression in one `erl` node
# (`erl_eval:exprs/2` inside a spawned process whose group leader is a sink, so
# no library output leaks into the result) and printing `~w`, i.e. the exact
# command quoted per line below.  The file is *data*: regenerate it, never
# hand-edit a value.
#
# `#`-prefixed and blank lines are ignored by the parser.
